speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the specific sectors that LTA is engaging with in its study on transporting workers by buses or other modes of transport; (b) how many companies in these sectors have been open to shifting to buses or other modes of transportation; (c) what are the specific pain points identified; and (d) what follow up steps will LTA be taking to address the pain points and scaling up the adoption of using buses and other modes of transportation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Transport what is the rationale for the ban under section 126 of the Road Traffic Act 1961 on carrying any person in or allowing any person to ride in goods vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We had on 5 July 2023 responded to the Member’s Adjournment Motion on the issue of transportation of workers on lorries and covered some of the points that he raised in the two Parliamentary Questions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As stated in our previous response, the Government shares the objective of enhancing safety for every worker, regardless of nationality.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have worked closely with stakeholders and introduced a suite of additional safety measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, we have mandated that the front passenger cabin be fully occupied before the rear deck can be used to carry workers, required lorries transporting workers to be fitted with canopies and higher side railings, raised requirements for S Pass and Work Permit holders to obtain a Singapore Class 3 licence that will allow them to drive light goods vehicles and imposed higher penalties for non-compliance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These measures have helped to enhance safety and reduce the risk for workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The average number of injured persons on board lorries has also gone down by about a third.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our efforts will focus on improving safety for all road users.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will also continue to roll out measures that address a multitude of factors behind accidents, such as driving behaviours and vehicle speed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government recognises that it is not ideal for workers to be transported on lorries, but we also understand the genuine concerns from employers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If the companies close down, there will be knock-on effects on society, including delays affecting new housing projects, polyclinics and Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) lines, as well as higher costs all around for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Their employees – both Singaporean and migrant workers – would also risk losing their jobs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We want to safeguard both the safety and livelihood of our workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: My Ministry has been working closely with relevant Government agencies, including the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), the Ministry of National Development (MND), the Building and Construction Authority (BCA), the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Traffic Police, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and Enterprise Singapore, as well as industry associations to progressively implement a suite of additional measures to improve safety for our workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, we introduced minimum rest time requirements for dual-role drivers, and we announced plans to require all lorries to be fitted with speed management devices, details of which will be announced by MHA later this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Traffic Police will also continue enforcement to ensure compliance with existing traffic regulations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are committed to improving safety for all road users and working with stakeholders, including the non-governmental organisations (NGOs), to develop practical solutions that are in the best interests of our workers, to protect their safety and their livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the Member’s other question, section 126 of the Road Traffic Act 1961, which regulates the carriage of persons in goods vehicles, is a legacy provision.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It has been in the Act since it was first passed in 1961.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: From legislative records, it is also found in the predecessor to the Act, the Road Traffic Ordinance, dating back to before 1950.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In my Adjournment Motion, I had asked to consider a timeline for a ban on the transportation of workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the reply is no, but could I take one step back and ask whether MOT will consider, at least, setting up a new work group comprising companies, including the SMEs and NGOs with the point of discussing whether we should have this timeline towards a ban on the transportation of workers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And as President Halimah has said in this House 14 years ago, when she was a Member of Parliament here: "We are talking about the lives and limbs of workers".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fourteen years later, we are still discussing how to resolve this problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Deputy Speaker Christopher de Souza had then, 14 years ago, also asked whether we would legislate to mandate that employers transport workers on buses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I really hope that we can have a greater sense of urgency; not an immediate ban but bearing in mind that we have talked about this for 14 years now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification is whether MOT can consider providing some funding or subsidies towards this transition towards safer modes of transport.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the constraints that SMEs face and I think the Government can provide a helping hand to them and also help the workers at the same time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say that his two supplementary questions were also covered in my reply to his Adjournment Motion last month.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But let me also reiterate that we have said that it is not ideal to transport workers on lorries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, we understand the concerns of the industry and, as Members have seen, they have laid it out in detail in a joint statement that they sent yesterday.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are real, practical and operational constraints for them to transit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, over the years, as I have said, we have been working very closely with the industry as well as with all stakeholders, the unions, for instance, and industry experts, to look at additional measures that we can put in place in order to improve safety for these workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for stating his concern for the workers' safety and also the NGOs who have submitted petitions expressing their concerns for these workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, we are all on the same page.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The industry associations – more than 20 of them – have also stated their commitment to improve and ensure the safety and welfare of the workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our commitment is to ensure the safety of all road users, including all our workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, the way forward is for us to continue to work closely together in order to look at practical solutions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Solutions which are implementable, workable at the ground, and in the best interests of the workers to protect their safety as well as their livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And as I have said, we have been doing this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also recently introduced a slate of measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The statistics themselves show that there has been impact and there has been improvement in terms of the number of injuries and fatalities of workers being transported on board lorries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Amongst all vehicle types, the highest proportion of injuries of people involved in road traffic accidents are motorcycles, at around 50% over the same period.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will remain our priority – the safety of all road users, including workers who are transported on lorries – and we will have to work closely with the industry to see how we can address some of these challenges and issues, encourage more to transit and also, at the same time, look at other measures that we can put in place, where feasible and effective, to enhance safety for the workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The other issue about working together, we have already said that we want to work together with everyone, including the NGOs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In fact, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) is equally concerned with the risk of ferrying workers on the back of lorries.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have mentioned this a few times inside and outside of this House.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am glad that the Government also shares the same concern.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I echo Member Louis Ng's suggestion to have a work group and NTUC would be very happy to be a part of the work group to look into both immediate solutions as well as longer-term solutions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Perhaps, the Ministry can consider, first, as an interim measure, prohibiting equipment, especially heavy equipment, and passengers on board the lorries at the same time because this causes a higher risk of injuries and fatalities in the event of an accident.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is something worth the Ministry's consideration as an interim measure to avoid serious injuries or even fatalities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we will continue to look at this and other suggestions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But the call now is for a new work group that will comprise the agencies, together with the companies, SMEs and NGOs, and perhaps NTUC as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Looking at this with new "lens" might enable us to come up with different solutions.
